title: Activation
description:
The deal's pinned terms as both agents sign them, and the struct the EscrowVault hashes into the deal id. It is returned inside the `funding` interaction's reply (§6.2) so a party can sign it, which is why it needs a published spelling: an agent that guesses wrong reads nulls and signs nothing.

Members are camelCase like every other object in this contract. A Runtime whose settlement layer or storage spells them otherwise MUST map them at the edge — the same rule §6.3 states for the proofs payload, and for the same reason.

CRITICAL: this renaming is a WIRE concern only. dealIdFor(Activation) hashes the EIP-712 struct in its ABI field ORDER (§4.4), not this JSON. Reordering members here, or treating the JSON key order as significant, changes nothing on chain — but a client that reconstructs the struct in the wrong ORDER derives a different deal id and its EIP-3009 authorization will be rejected at fund() time. The field order that matters is the one below, and it is frozen.

termsHash.description: The accepted contract's content anchor — the same 32-byte digest the coordination layer carries, in either of two accepted spellings. `sha256:<hex>` is what the coordination layer uses and what a Runtime normally emits here; `0x<hex>` is the settlement layer's spelling. A consumer MUST accept both and compare digest-to-digest after stripping the prefix, because the prefix is not part of the ABI encoding: only the 32 bytes are hashed into the deal id.

buyer.description:
The buyer's WALLET address — the account the EIP-3009 authorization moves funds from, not the buyer agent's DID or runtime key.

OPTIONAL here, and its absence is a normal stage rather than an error: the Runtime assembles the Activation before it knows the wallet, and this member is filled from the buyer's own funding submission (§6.2.1 role binding — only the buyer may set it). A `funding` read before that submission returns the Activation without it. Both parties MUST therefore treat an Activation lacking `buyer` as NOT YET SIGNABLE: the deal id derives from the completed struct, so signing a partial one produces a signature against a deal id that will never exist on chain.

buyerAgent.description: The buyer agent's runtime key as an EVM address (§8). The vault verifies party signatures against these addresses, so they are addresses here rather than DIDs.

sellerPayout.description: Where a successful settlement pays. Taken from the contract's escrow.payoutAddress: a deal cannot be proposed without one, because the engine cannot settle fixed_outcome without a destination.

arbiter.description: The contract-named arbiter's address. The only signer the vault accepts for a resolution.

amount.description: The escrowed amount in the asset's base units, as a DECIMAL STRING. It is a string because a uint256 does not survive JSON's number type — a client that parses it into a float loses precision and derives a different deal id. v1 settles USDC only, so these are 6-decimal base units.

fundingDeadline.description: Absolute deadline for funding to confirm on chain. Passing it moves COMMITTED to EXPIRED (§3.1).

deliveryConfirmationWindow.description: How long the buyer has to accept or reject after delivery. On expiry the deal auto-confirms to ACCEPTED — silence is acceptance, which is why this value is inside the signed struct rather than a Runtime policy knob.

arbitrationWindow.description: How long the arbiter has after an appeal. On expiry anyone may refund the buyer — the exit that keeps DISPUTED from being a state with no way out when an arbiter loses its key, since the vault has no owner and no sweep.

durationSeconds.description: A duration in seconds, relative to the window's own start — not an absolute time.
